title: Pilot deployment matrix and customer scenario playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note is a practical playbook for Solutions Engineering to use during customer pilots where the core question is: which deployment mode (hosted, dedicated, private) or combination best satisfies the customer constraints for latency, cost, data sovereignty, and operational ownership. It complements the higher-level tradeoff docs and focuses on scenario-driven decision criteria, a lightweight decision matrix SEs can run through in a 60–90 minute workshop, and an execution checklist for a 6–8 week pilot.

Audience:
- SEs running customer pilots
- Product managers validating hosting constraints
- Infra owners who will support Dedicated or Private onboarding

Quick summary recommendation pattern (tl;dr):
- Start with a narrow hosted pilot when the customer needs quick time-to-value, lower initial cost, and permissive data policies. Use hosted for functional validation and latency profiling.
- If predictable throughput or stronger isolation is required, transition to a short Dedicated canary phase with pinned capacity and a constrained SLA.
- If data sovereignty, full auditability, or air-gapped operation is mandated, plan a parallel Private pilot early (parallel to Dedicated canary) to validate network, KMS/HSM, and observability integrations.

Decision matrix (workshop-friendly):
Run through these axes; mark scores 1–5 (1 = low importance/impact for this customer, 5 = must-have). After scoring, weight the axes per customer and compute a simple weighted sum. SEs: carry a printed copy of this matrix into the workshop.
- Latency SLO (p95 target in ms)
- Throughput (reqs/sec and burst behavior)
- Data residency / sovereignty constraints
- Data privacy / PII handling obligations
- Compliance & auditability (retention of logs, access control)
- Cost sensitivity / target unit economics
- Operational ownership preference (managed vs self-run)
- Integration complexity (on-prem systems, private APIs)
- Risk tolerance for degradations or fallback scenarios

Common scoring outcomes and pragmatic pipelines:
- High latency sensitivity (p95 < 120ms) + low data restrictions: Hosted + edge routing + regional model placement. If p95 can't be met, re-evaluate model size/quantization or move to Dedicated in-region nodes.
- Predictable high throughput + enterprise isolation: Dedicated reservation (GPU pool), canary with traffic-splitting, increase pre-warmed KV cache.
- Strict sovereignty or offline operation: Private (VPC or on-prem). Run a limited data-plane-only Private pilot (control plane optionally still managed) to validate network egress rules and KMS integration.
- Mixed constraints (e.g., low-latency for a subset of users + sensitive logs): Hybrid split routing (sensitive requests -> Private in-region; general requests -> Hosted).

Playbook: 6–8 week pilot (fast path)
Week 0 (prep):
- Align on success metrics (latency p95, per-req cost, availability, regression targets on sample prompts).
- Inventory data flows and identify PII endpoints.
- Agreement on what constitutes production-ready (e.g., SLOs, monitoring coverage).
- Provision minimal infra: hosted API keys, test Dedicated quota, or sandbox Private cluster as applicable.

Week 1–2 (functional validation on hosted):
- Implement core integration against Redwood hosted API. Capture latency traces and token breakdowns.
- Run synthetic load and sample prompts to measure model behavior and quality.
- Identify prompt-level regressions and record golden prompts for later regression tests.

Week 3–4 (scale and isolation tests):
- If throughput or isolation is required, spin up a Dedicated canary. Mirror production traffic subset (5–10%).
- Validate autoscaling configuration, burst capacity, and prewarming.
- If Private is required, start network validation: VPC peering, route tables, firewall rules, and KMS handshake.

Week 5–6 (observability + robustness):
- Enable trace-level observability: per-request traces, token cost, latency, KV cache hit rates.
- Run chaos tests (node drain, network latency injection) to verify fallback policies (e.g., burst route to Hosted or lower-cost model variant).
- Confirm runbooks for escalations and SLA breaches.

Week 7–8 (handoff & go/no-go):
- Compile pilot report: metric comparisons (hosted vs dedicated vs private runs), cost projection for steady-state, and risk register.
- If moving to Dedicated or Private, schedule a staged rollout plan (canary -> 20% -> 50% -> full) and rollback criteria.

Operational tradeoffs and knobs to tune during pilot:
- Batching: greater batching reduces unit cost but increases tail latency. For low p95 targets, prefer small batch sizes + aggressive latency SLAs.
- KV/prefix caching: big wins for repeated or conversational workloads; verify cache-hit telemetry early.
- Quantization profiles: test INT8/4 quantized variants in sandbox to measure quality delta before using in Dedicated or Private.
- Model variant routing: maintain a smaller, cheaper variant as an automatic fallback when capacity is constrained.

Security and compliance checklist (minimum to validate during pilot):
- Data flow map with PII annotation.
- KMS integration smoke test (rotate keys, verify access denial).
- Audit log retention in requested region; export to customer SIEM if required.
- Role-based access control mapping for SE, infra, and customer admins.
- Pen test scope agreement if Private/on-prem will host sensitive models.

Instrumentation and metrics (must-haves):
- Latency percentiles (p50, p90, p95, p99), per-model and per-route
- Token cost per request and per-conversation
- KV cache hit ratio and cache TTLs
- CPU/GPU utilization on Dedicated/Private nodes
- Error rates by class (rate-limit, infra, model timeout, model error)
- Quality regression indicator: mismatch rate vs golden prompts

Customer conversation scripts (snippets SEs can use):
- When customer says “we need absolute control of the data": "Can you describe the specific regulatory or audit requirements? Often we can meet the controls with a VPC-backed Private pilot or with Dedicated plus log segregation — let's map the exact evidence you need and pick the smallest surface that satisfies it."
- When customer says "we can’t tolerate any latency >200ms": "Let's instrument a hosted prototype to measure baseline. If we can't meet on hosted, we move to regional Dedicated nodes and tune batching and cache. We also prepare a fallback cheaper model that keeps availability if the primary model exceeds latency thresholds."

Runbook excerpts (one-liners for SEs):
- If p95 spikes > target for 5 minutes: check model queue length -> if >threshold, divert new requests to fallback model variant and notify infra on-call.
- If cache hit ratio drops >20%: increase TTL or investigate prefix variance in prompts.
- If Dedicated node OOMs on startup: reduce max_seq_len and set smaller batch cap, reinit with quantized weights for node.

Unresolved questions to capture during customer kickoff (use these to push for decisions):
- Which legal entity's data center must host logs for compliance?
- Is the control plane permitted to be outside customer network for Private deployment?
- What is the expected request distribution window (10% of traffic in 1-hour bursts or uniform)?

Appendix: example lightweight config fragment (for SE reference only)
- routing_policy:
    name: low-latency-first
    priorities: [regionally-pinned-dedicated, hosted, fallback-model]
    latency_threshold_ms: 120
- model_profiles:
    - name: big-llm-prod
      variant: quantized-int8
      max_seq: 2048
      warm_cache: true

Notes, post-pilot artifacts to produce:
- Pilot summary (1-pager): metrics, cost delta, compliance gaps, go/no-go recommendation.
- Runbook for chosen production path (Hosted-only OR Dedicated-runbook OR Private-install play).
- Regression suite with golden prompts and automated daily checks.

Observations from recent pilots (lessons learned):
- Customers overestimate the effort to integrate with hosted control plane — a quick demo cuts that friction.
- Early KV cache tuning often yields 20–40% token-cost improvements without quality loss.
- Network egress rules are the most common blocker in Private pilots — create a standard network checklist to accelerate networking signoff.

Action items (for SE running next pilot):
- [ ] Book 60–90 minute decision-matrix workshop with customer (invite infra and security).
- [ ] Provision sandbox hosted keys + small Dedicated quota before kickoff.
- [ ] Collect 50 representative prompts from customer for golden set.
- [ ] Agree on SLOs and monitoring exports (CloudWatch/Prometheus/SIEM).
- [ ] Schedule a mid-pilot review (end of Week 3).

End of document.

Owners: Aisha Kaur (SE lead), Benji Morales (infra liaison), Claire Zhang (security).
